chapter: The Cold War Era and Bipolarity
trick: The Cold War was a contest between two blocs that never fought each other directly — that is why it is 'cold'. Attach each alliance to its side: NATO 1949 is the Western bloc, the Warsaw Pact 1955 the Soviet. Its opening is usually dated to 1945-47 and its close to the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the Soviet collapse in 1991.

trick: Non-alignment is not neutrality and not isolation — it means judging each issue on its merits rather than joining a bloc. Five founders: Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah. The first summit was at Belgrade in 1961, and Bandung 1955 was the conference that prepared the ground.

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the Non-Aligned Movement.

items.statement: Non-alignment means staying neutral and taking no position on world affairs.
items.why: It means not joining either bloc while judging each issue on its merits — an active foreign policy, not a passive one.

items.statement: The first NAM summit was held at Belgrade in 1961.
items.why: Twenty-five countries attended, hosted by Tito.

items.statement: The Bandung Conference of 1955 preceded and prepared for NAM.
items.why: The Afro-Asian conference in Indonesia established the ground of Afro-Asian solidarity.

items.statement: Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah are counted as the founders.
items.why: India, Yugoslavia, Egypt, Indonesia and Ghana respectively.

items.statement: NAM demanded a New International Economic Order.
items.why: From the 1970s the movement's emphasis shifted from security to economic justice between the North and the South.

chapter: The United Nations and its Organs
trick: Six principal organs, and the Security Council is the one that matters in questions: 15 members, of whom 5 are permanent — the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia and China — and each permanent member holds the veto. The General Assembly has every member with one vote each, but its resolutions are recommendations.

trick: Panchsheel means five principles, agreed with China in 1954: mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. The number five and the year 1954 travel together — and the 1962 war with China is what makes the agreement so often asked about.
